req_desc: The schema holds seven tables with UTC timestamps.
Every seeded account with its password is written into `/app/USER_README.md`.
The `accounts` table records `id`, `email`, `password_hash`, `role`, `created_at` ...
The `case_studies` table records `slug`, `title`, `index_title`, `template`, `client`, `year`, `published`, `published_at` ...
The `case_study_disciplines` table holds at least one discipline per case study, none twice.
The `chapters` table records `anchor`, `rail_label`, `heading`, `body`, `position` ...
The `media` table records `role`, `object_key`, `content_type`, `byte_size`, `sha256`, `width`, `height`, `alt_text` ...
The `reading_list` table records `max_fraction`, `last_fraction`, `chapters_read`, `last_seen`, with `completed` computed on read ...
The `preferences` table records `motion_level`, `level_source`, `reveal_all` per account ...
Choosing a motion level stores the level with `level_source` of `chosen` ...
The eleven published case studies are seeded with the catalogue values ...
The product has one designer, no team, no second tenant, no designer signup.
The product has no search, comments, likes, sharing, newsletter, chat, payment.
The product has no contact form of any kind.
The product has no light theme, no theme switch.
Navigating between routes is a full page load.
The product shows no cookie banner beyond the one browser question, no consent manager.
The product has no third-party analytics, no tracking identifier, no external call at run time.
The build ships zero binary assets, naming the licensed fonts without shipping them.
Two discipline marks are absent rather than invented.
The app is reachable at `APP_PUBLIC_URL` ...
The HTTP API is served on the same origin under the `/api` prefix.
`GET /api/health` returns `200` once the app is ready.
The app starts from the environment image with no manual steps.
Login credentials are written to `/app/USER_README.md`.
Reserved `.browser_screenshots/` plus `.downloads/` directories exist at the app root, empty.
The app serves a production build, never a dev server.
The server keeps running after the session ends, not a child of the shell.
The server binds `0.0.0.0`.
The app never downloads, installs, compiles or starts a copy of a backing service.
The app uses only the named providers with no edge functions.
The app uses no persistent volumes, no fixed container names, no custom networks.
`POST /api/auth/signup` takes `email` plus a `password` of at least `8` characters, returning the created `reader` with an `access_token`.
`POST /api/auth/login` returns the account with an `access_token`.
`GET /api/me` returns the signed-in account's `id`, `email`, `role`.
`POST /api/consent` takes `choice` of `yes` or `no`.
`GET /api/case-studies` returns `slug`, `title`, `index_title`, `client`, `product`, `disciplines`, `year`, `year_end`, `ongoing`, `template`, `home_placement` per published case study ...
`GET /api/case-studies/{slug}` returns `chapters` with `anchor`, `rail_label`, `heading` ...
The related endpoint returns exactly two published case studies, slot one first, whenever at least three are published ...
`GET /api/filters` returns `clients` plus `disciplines`, each entry carrying `token` with `label`.
`GET /api/reading-list` returns the caller's entries newest first, each with `slug`, `title`, `saved_at`, `max_fraction`, `last_fraction`, `chapters_read`, `completed`, `last_seen`.
`POST /api/reading-list` takes `slug`.
`DELETE /api/reading-list/{slug}` removes the entry.
`PUT /api/reading-list/{slug}/progress` takes `fraction` plus `chapters`.
`PUT /api/preferences` takes `motion_level` or `reveal_all`.
`GET /api/studio/case-studies` returns every case study with `id`, `slug`, `index_title`, `published`.
`POST /api/studio/case-studies` returns the created case study unpublished with an `id` ...
`GET /api/studio/case-studies/{id}` returns a draft in full to the designer.
`PATCH /api/studio/case-studies/{id}` updates an editable field.
`POST /api/studio/case-studies/{id}/chapters` takes `anchor`, `rail_label`, `heading`, `body`, returning the created chapter.
`DELETE /api/studio/chapters/{id}` removes a chapter.
`POST /api/studio/case-studies/{id}/media` takes `file`, `role`, `alt_text`, `width`, `height`, returning the `object_key`.
`POST /api/studio/case-studies/{id}/publish` publishes the case study.
`POST /api/studio/case-studies/{id}/unpublish` returns the case study to draft.
A list endpoint returns a top-level JSON array ...
Bytes held in memory, on the app disk, in a base64 column, or in a public bucket are a contract violation ...
`GET /api/preferences` returns `motion_level`, `level_source`, `reveal_all`.
